# jumpcloud_user (Resource)

Manages a JumpCloud user. Use it for accounts that no other system owns, such as test and service accounts; people are created and updated by the HR integration, which would undo changes made here. The provider does not set passwords: set one in the admin console or have the user activate their account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A test account for synthetic sign-in checks. People come from the HR integration.
resource "jumpcloud_user" "synthetic_test" {
  username   = "synthetic.test"
  email      = "synthetic.test@example.com"
  first_name = "Synthetic"
  last_name  = "Test"
  department = "Engineering"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) Email address.
- `username` (String) Username.

### Optional

- `attributes` (Map of String) Custom attributes by name. Kept as is when not set; `{}` removes them all.
- `department` (String) Department, which dynamic group rules can match as `user.user_department`.
- `first_name` (String) First name.
- `job_title` (String) Job title, which dynamic group rules can match as `user.user_job_title`.
- `last_name` (String) Last name.
- `state` (String) Account state: `ACTIVATED`, `STAGED`, or `SUSPENDED`. When not set, a new user gets the organization's default state and an existing one keeps its state.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) User ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by ID.
terraform import jumpcloud_user.synthetic_test 5f0c1b2a3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d
```
